coordinate_system: Godot metres: route points are [x,z,height]; shore sections are [z,toe_x,bench_x,bench_height]
status: Implementation control proposal, not visual approval. Sculpt actual connected roadbeds and broad grass banks; assess the resulting game views.
implementation_rules: Protect existing sand/sea floor at height <= 0.25 m; if a toe falls in that protected zone, fade the bank into existing ground rather than moving the protected vertex.

Sculpt road longitudinal grade and transverse bed first; derive surface roles from final geometry and use worn centers, rooted grass shoulders, isolated exposed soil, and sand only near the actual beach.
Main routes share exact junction endpoints. Union roadbeds at their junctions and blend grades; do not layer independent crossing strips.
Court masks must not repaint or flatten the short stair approaches. Entry approaches override general court grades outside protected stair/floor footprints.
All actual building floors, porch slabs, stair treads and foundation supports are protected. Entry endpoints stop before the lowest tread face; use the exact existing support heights at contacts.
Do not make an all-coast exposed brown soil apron. Broad banks carry grass down toward the beach, with local bare wear near real circulation and modest toe transitions.

Only two deliberate main beach descents: Trade pier at z9 and shared work-pier descent ending near z38. Connect the z38 and z43 piers by existing low beach circulation without painting another narrow dark road stripe.

Diner-Sari saddle requires actual terrain fill: current [13,53] is about 0.311 m, target 1.16 m. Fill and connect the two courts, retaining a grass bank beachward; do not leave a sand tongue between them.

Tavern frontage is spatially constrained by high porch over x10.74..11.24, z38.5..43.1. Retain one short explicit supporting cut bank beachward of the road around z38..42.7; do not claim this region is a broad gentle grass bank.
Reground whole semantic plant, furniture and supply groups after terrain deformation. Do not select objects solely by loose spatial bounding boxes.
